item.title: Hangul, Sounds, and Greetings
item.description: Lesson 1: Hangul, Sounds, and Greetings Korean is written in Hangul, an alphabet created in the 15th century that is systematic enough to learn in a focused session, and learning it from the start — rather than relying only on romanisation — pays off in every later lesson. item.title: 입니다, 있어요/없어요, and Describing Yourself
item.description: Lesson 2: 입니다, 있어요/없어요, and Describing Yourself Korean sentences end with the verb, and the copula (the "to be" verb) changes with politeness level. item.title: Present Tense Verbs and Word Order
item.description: Lesson 3: Present Tense Verbs and Word Order Korean verb stems end in a vowel or consonant, and the polite informal present adds -아요/-어요 (or -해요 for 하다 verbs) according to vowel harmony: if the last vowel of the stem is ㅏ or ㅗ, use -아요; otherwise use -어요. item.title: Numbers, Counters, and Time
item.description: Lesson 4: Numbers, Counters, and Time Korean has two number systems, and using the wrong one is the most recognisable beginner error. Sino-Korean numbers (from Chinese) are used for money, dates, phone numbers, addresses, and minutes: 일 (il, 1), 이 (i, 2), 삼 (sam, 3), 사 (sa, 4), 오 (o, 5), 육 (yuk…

item.title: Past and Future Tenses
item.description: Lesson 5: Past and Future Tenses The Korean past tense in the polite informal style adds -았어요/-었어요 (or -했어요 for 하다 verbs) to the stem, following the same vowel harmony as the present: if the last vowel is ㅏ or ㅗ, use -았어요; otherwise use -었어요. item.title: Food, Ordering, and Quantities
item.description: Lesson 6: Food, Ordering, and Quantities Korean food vocabulary is immediately usable, and restaurant language rewards a few polite set phrases. item.title: Future Plans, Modal Expressions, and the Weather
item.description: Lesson 7: Future Plans, Modal Expressions, and the Weather Korean expresses ability, permission, obligation, and desire with set patterns built on the verb stem, and learning them as patterns — rather than as separate verbs — is the fastest route to useful speech.
